command:
set -eu
TESTDIR=/run/ssh-host-cert-test
rm -rf "$TESTDIR"
mkdir -m 700 "$TESTDIR"
ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C 'temporary host-certificate verification key' -f "$TESTDIR/id"
mkdir -p /root/.ssh
chmod 700 /root/.ssh
if [ -e /root/.ssh/authorized_keys ]; then cp -a /root/.ssh/authorized_keys "$TESTDIR/authorized_keys.saved"; else : > "$TESTDIR/no-authorized-keys"; fi
cleanup() {
  if [ -e "$TESTDIR/authorized_keys.saved" ]; then cp -a "$TESTDIR/authorized_keys.saved" /root/.ssh/authorized_keys; else rm -f /root/.ssh/authorized_keys; fi
  rm -rf "$TESTDIR"
}
trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM
cat "$TESTDIR/id.pub" >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
restorecon -RF /root/.ssh 2>/dev/null || true
CA_KEY=$(cat /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ca.pub)
printf '@cert-authority %s,%s %s\n' "$NODE_NAME" "$NODE_IP" "$CA_KEY" > "$TESTDIR/known_hosts"
chmod 600 "$TESTDIR/known_hosts"
set +e
ssh -v -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile="$TESTDIR/known_hosts" -o GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o HostKeyAlgorithms=ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i "$TESTDIR/id" root@"$NODE_IP" 'printf "remote_host=%s remote_boot_id=" "$(hostname)"; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id' > "$TESTDIR/client.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e
grep -E 'Server host certificate:|Host .+ is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate|Found CA key|Authenticated to|remote_host=' "$TESTDIR/client.log" || true
printf 'ssh_exit=%s\n' "$RC"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ]
